question: Which of the following best describes conservation of momentum in collisions?
options: Heavier objects always gain momentum in collisions.
Total momentum is conserved in collisions without external impulses.
Momentum is conserved only when objects stick together.
Kinetic energy is always conserved in every collision.
gold_answer: Total momentum is conserved in collisions without external impulses.
notes: Team-authored original item on conservation of momentum in collisions. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Momentum is conserved only when objects stick together.

claims.text: The total momentum of the system before impact equals its total after impact.

evidence.text: With no external impulse during the brief impact, the vector sum of momenta is unchanged from before to after.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states the vector sum is unchanged, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Two objects can collide without exerting forces on each other.

evidence.text: Collisions act through equal and opposite contact forces, as required by the third law of motion.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage requires contact forces in every collision, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Seatbelts are unnecessary at low speeds.

evidence.text: Injury outcomes were stratified by speed band in the crash registry.

claims.verdict_rationale: Stratifying outcomes cannot show seatbelts are unnecessary, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Kinetic energy is always conserved in every collision.

claims.text: In an elastic collision, kinetic energy is also conserved.

evidence.text: Ideal elastic collisions store impact energy temporarily in deformation and return it fully, preserving kinetic energy.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes full return of impact energy, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Momentum conservation fails at low speeds.

evidence.text: Momentum conservation holds at all everyday speeds; only near light speed does the relativistic form take over.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage affirms conservation at everyday speeds, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Crumple zones increase the force on passengers.

evidence.text: Injury rates were compared between vehicle models with different front-end designs.

claims.verdict_rationale: Comparing injury rates cannot show crumple zones increase force, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Heavier objects always gain momentum in collisions.

claims.text: Recoil occurs because momentum lost by one object is gained by another.

evidence.text: A launcher gains backward momentum exactly balancing the forward momentum carried away by the projectile.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes exactly balancing momenta, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Friction with the ground never affects collision analysis.

evidence.text: External impulses such as friction change total momentum, so real analyses must account for or minimize them.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states friction changes total momentum, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Airbags work by speeding up the collision.

evidence.text: Head injury readings were logged in crash tests with and without airbags.

claims.verdict_rationale: Logging readings cannot show airbags speed up collisions, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
